messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (faithfulness) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is every claim in the brief supported by the cited evidence and the fact sheet, with nothing overstated and no cited contrary evidence left out? Pass means yes.
Fail on an uncited claim, a number that is off the fact sheet, a scope wider than the cited accounts, a paraphrase placed in quotation marks, or an ignored contrary citation.
The evidence is the brief, the cited insights and the fact sheet (accounts, ARR, mentions, routes, renewals).
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "brief": "## Problem\nStaff cannot confidently adjust reserves because it's unclear which roles are permitted to do so, especially before payment triggers. This creates risk of unauthorized changes and undermines trust in reserve accuracy.\n\n## Who is affected\n- Sales teams, who have raised this topic in 2 accounts [i:8b9b09ae561d0188][i:f6f76c5dbb558280].\n\n## Evidence\n- This topic has been mentioned 2 times across 2 accounts [i:8b9b09ae561d0188][i:f6f76c5dbb558280].\n- The feedback has come via 1 route: sales [i:8b9b09ae561d0188][i:f6f76c5dbb558280].\n- The total ARR from accounts mentioning this topic is £1,600,000 [i:8b9b09ae561d0188].\n- There has been 1 renewal in the last 90 days.\n- A customer from Marrowgate Commercial stated, I also want to make sure roles are assigned correctly so only authorized staff can adjust reserves. [i:8b9b09ae561d0188].\n- A customer from Harrowfield Fleet Mutual stated, That’s exactly what I’m after — especially how roles affect who can adjust those reserves before payment triggers. [i:f6f76c5dbb558280].\n\n## Why now\n- The topic has been raised by two separate accounts in recent months, with mentions in September and October 2026 [i:f6f76c5dbb558280][i:8b9b09ae561d0188].\n- One of the affected accounts, Marrowgate Commercial, is due for renewal on 2026-12-12 [i:8b9b09ae561d0188].",
 "cited_insights": [
  {
   "id": "8b9b09ae561d0188",
   "quote": "I also want to make sure roles are assigned correctly so only authorized staff can adjust reserves.",
   "account": "Marrowgate Commercial",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-06T15:02:00Z"
  },
  {
   "id": "f6f76c5dbb558280",
   "quote": "That’s exactly what I’m after — especially how roles affect who can adjust those reserves before payment triggers.",
   "account": "Harrowfield Fleet Mutual",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-09-22T12:46:00Z"
  }
 ],
 "fact_sheet": {
  "as_of": "2026-11-03",
  "accounts_n": 2,
  "mentions_n": 2,
  "routes_n": 1,
  "mentions_by_route": {
   "sales": 2
  },
  "arr_total_gbp": 1600000.0,
  "renewals_90d_n": 1,
  "accounts": [
   {
    "name": "Marrowgate Commercial",
    "arr_gbp": 1600000.0,
    "renewal_date": "2026-12-12",
    "mentions": 1
   },
   {
    "name": "Harrowfield Fleet Mutual",
    "arr_gbp": null,
    "renewal_date": null,
    "mentions": 1
   }
  ]
 }
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The quotes from Marrowgate Commercial and Harrowfield Fleet Mutual match the cited insights verbatim, and the mention count (2), account count (2), route count (1), ARR (£1,600,000), and renewal count (1) all match the fact sheet. However, the 'Who is affected' section claims 'Sales teams, who have raised this topic' — the citations show the feedback arrived via the sales route, not that sales teams are the affected users; the quotes themselves indicate claims-handling staff are the ones concerned about reserve permissions. This misattributes who raised and is affected by the issue, overstating the cited evidence.", "verdict": "fail"}
